title: PRD: Quantization & Fidelity Experimentation Lab
author: Ivy Chen
content:
Summary:
This PRD defines the Quantization & Fidelity Experimentation Lab (the Lab): a reproducible, service-backed environment for running targeted fidelity experiments when introducing quantized model variants, pruning, or other cost-saving serving techniques. The Lab's outputs are deterministic experiment artifacts, decision signals (pass/fail/gated), and standardized reports used by Product, Applied ML, and Serving Runtime to decide rollouts and fallback strategies.

Goals:
- Provide a single source of truth for fidelity impact of any automated compression or quantization profile across representative tenant workloads.
- Produce machine-readable experiment results (quality deltas, latency/cost deltas, statistical significance) and a human-readable report with recommended rollout gating (allow, canary, block).
- Support experiment types: full-model quantization, per-layer mixed-precision, activation pruning, low-rank adapters, and forced KV-cache eviction behaviors.
- Integrate with the Optimize and Serving Runtime rollout pipelines to automatically recommend safe rollouts and guardrail thresholds.

Non-goals:
- The Lab will not itself perform live production A/B rollouts. It produces evidence and artifacts consumed by the rollout systems.
- The Lab does not replace long-term model quality monitoring (that remains in Console/Optimize).

Success metrics (first 6 months):
- 90% of candidate quantization profiles produce a deterministic Lab report within 48 hours of submission (on standard profiles).
- >=75% reduction in manual evaluation time for quantization-related rollouts (measured via engineering survey).
- Fallbacks triggered by Lab-approved rollback policies reduce customer-seen quality regressions by >60% vs ad-hoc rollouts.

Stakeholders and owners:
- Product (owner): Ivy Chen (product lead) — defines acceptance criteria and experimental matrix templates.
- Applied ML (owner): Rafael Ortega — curates evaluation sets and quality metrics per workload/domain.
- Eng: Serving Runtime (owner): Arjun Malhotra — provides runtime hooks and cost/latency telemetry, implements automated rollout integration.
- Eng: DevEx — SDK/CLI for experiment submission and artifacts retrieval.

User stories:
1) As an Applied ML engineer, I want to submit a quantization profile and a list of evaluation prompt sets and receive a standardized fidelity report (metrics, significance, artifact links) so I can recommend rollout policy.
2) As a Product manager, I want a summary dashboard showing pass/fail across customer segments, so I can prioritize safe rollouts.
3) As an SRE, I want experiment artifacts to include traceable request IDs and telemetry so I can audit regressions that reach production.

Experiment runner requirements (functional):
- Accept experiment definitions as YAML or JSON via SDK/REST and return a job id.
- Run experiments against: canonical test harness (deterministic RNG seeds), a configurable subset of model variants (float32, int8, 4-bit mixed), and a set of workload slices (chat, code, long-form completion, embeddings).
- Capture and persist: per-example outputs, token-level latencies, resource utilization (GPU RAM, kernels used), and per-example quality scores.
- Produce a structured report containing: aggregated metrics (mean, median, p99), delta vs baseline, 95% confidence intervals, A/B test p-values, and an automated pass/fail recommendation based on policy.

Experiment runner requirements (non-functional):
- Turnaround: typical small experiments complete within 24 - 48 hours; pilot-level experiments (large prompt sets) within 5 days.
- Reproducibility: experiments run with immutable seeds, pinned model binaries, and environment hashes.
- Multi-tenant safety: experiments run in an isolated namespace, with no customer data used unless explicitly authorized and scrubbed.

Quality metrics and gating logic:
- Primary metrics per workload:
  - Chat/Completion: semantic similarity (embedding cosine) vs baseline, normalized F1 when applicable, and response length parity. Gate: mean embedding cosine drop <= 0.012 AND 99th-percentile semantic delta <= 0.02.
  - Code generation: pass@k and compilation success rate. Gate: pass@1 drop <= 1.5 percentage points and compile-failure delta <= 0.5pp.
  - Embeddings: mean cosine similarity drop <= 0.015; downstream retrieval MAP drop <= 0.8%.
  - Latency/Cost: p50 latency must not increase more than 8% for the target serving configuration; cost/unit must be reduced by >= 12% to be considered.
- Automated pass/fail decision algorithm:
  1. Compute per-workload deltas and CIs.
  2. If any primary metric breaches gate thresholds -> FAIL.
  3. If primary metrics pass but secondary metrics (edge-case slices) show regressions above 95th-percentile thresholds -> WARN (manual review).
  4. Produce recommendation: allow | canary (10% traffic) | block.

Experiment definition schema (example YAML):
  ---
  experiment_name: "int4-mixed-prune-v2"
  model_variant: "redwood-open-7b-v2"
  baseline_variant: "redwood-open-7b-fp16"
  profiles:
    - name: "int4-mixed"
      quantization: "mixed-int4"
      per_layer_overrides: ["attn-16:8", "mlp-5:4"]
  workload_slices:
    - name: "customer-chat-small"
      sample_set: "canonical/chat-1000"
      metrics: ["embed_cosine","mean_length","toxicity_rate"]
  eval_repeat: 3
  rng_seed: 41321

Telemetry and artifact requirements:
- Events captured: experiment.submitted, experiment.started, example.{id}.inference.start, example.{id}.inference.end, experiment.completed, experiment.report.generated.
- Telemetry must include: job_id, model_variant, profile_hash, seed, environment_hash, worker_version, and timestamps.
- Artifacts stored: raw outputs (per example), normalized metric table (CSV), aggregated report (JSON and human-readable markdown), and an immutable experiment metadata file.

Data handling and PII policy:
- No customer PII may be used in Lab experiments unless explicitly consented and processed in a restricted workspace.
- When customer data is approved, the Lab will apply automated scrubbing per the Data Management policy: remove names, tokens matching credit-card patterns, and PII heuristics.

Integration points and automation:
- Rollout Integration: Lab will call the Rollout Recommendation API with pass/canary/block and attach experiment artifact links. Serving Runtime will annotate model variants with experiment ids.
- Console: Add a new page type "Experiment Report" where product and applied-ml can browse experiments, filter by model, and export PDFs.
- CLI: redwood-lab submit --file experiment.yaml -> returns job id; redwood-lab report --id JOB -> downloads artifacts.

Operational requirements and infra sizing:
- Baseline test cluster: 8x A100(80GB) equivalent nodes for parallel small experiments; ability to burst to 32 nodes for large sweeps.
- Storage: lifecycle retention of experiment artifacts: 90 days hot, 1 year cold archive.
- RBAC: roles: lab-admin, lab-runner, lab-viewer. lab-runner may execute jobs but cannot delete artifacts.

Reporting and human-readable output (example):
Title: int4-mixed-prune-v2 — redwood-open-7b-v2
Summary: Pass with WARN on edge-case legal prompts. p50 latency -3.4%, cost/unit -18.7%
Primary metrics table:
| workload | baseline | variant | delta | CI95 | decision |
| chat-1000 | 0.872 | 0.861 | -0.011 | ±0.003 | PASS |
| legal-slice | 0.790 | 0.760 | -0.030 | ±0.010 | WARN |
Notes: The legal-slice regression is concentrated in documents with very long citations (see artifact: /artifacts/12345/legal-edge-cases.csv). Recommend a canary to 5% with automated fallback to fp16 for flagged tenant tags.

Rollout gating workflow (recommended):
1. Experiment authorates PRD + attaches Lab report.
2. Applied ML reviews WARNs; if minor, mark canary; if block, require engineer to iterate.
3. If canary approved, schedule a 2-week canary at 5-10% traffic with monitoring alerts configured (quality delta, token-level fraud checks).
4. If canary succeeds (no production quality regression for 14 days), promote to gradual rollout.

Testing, QA, and guardrails:
- Unit tests: experiment runner validation logic, schema conformance.
- Integration tests: end-to-end run against a small synthetic workload with deterministic outputs.
- Chaos test: randomly kill runner nodes; verify retry semantics and artifact integrity.
- Guardrails: experiments that touch PII require approval from Data Governance.

Open questions and risks:
- How to budget the infra cost of large sweep experiments vs. business value? (Mitigation: quota-based submission and cost-credits workflow.)
- Potential overfitting to canonical prompt sets. (Mitigation: require at least one customer representative slice for any production rollout.)

Milestones and roadmap (quarterly):
- Q1: MVP experiment runner, CLI, and basic report generation; integrate with Rollout Recommendation API.
- Q2: Support for mixed-precision per-layer overrides, artifact retention policy, and Console report UI.
- Q3: Auto-recommendations tied to Optimize insights (cost/latency tradeoff visualizer) and canary orchestration link.

Appendix: example CLI usage and minimal SDK snippet
# Submit
redwood-lab submit --file int4-experiment.yaml
# Poll
redwood-lab status --id job-20270322-001
# Fetch report
redwood-lab report --id job-20270322-001 --output ./reports/job-001

Python SDK (pseudo):
from redwood.lab import LabClient
client = LabClient()
job = client.submit(experiment_definition)
report = client.wait_and_fetch(job.id)
print(report.summary)
